chunks: (2) Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated to us, he said: My father al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Aamir narrated to me, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Jumhur, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from al-Fadl ibn Yasar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, Exalted is He: 'The Day We will call every people with their Imam. And whoever is given his record in his right hand - those will read their record and will not be wronged at all.' He said: 'O Fadhl, know your Imam, for if you know your Imam, it will not harm you whether this matter (the appearance of the Qa'im) comes early or late. And whoever knows his Imam and then dies before the one of this matter rises, he is like the one who is sitting in his camp, nay, he is like the one who sat under his banner.' (He said) And some of our companions narrated it with this addition: '...like the one who was martyred with the Messenger of Allah.'

key_terms.صَاحِبُ هَذَا الْأَمْرِ: The Master of this Command (referring to Imam al-Mahdi)

ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic verse 'We will call every people with their Imam' mean in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam al-Sadiq (as) clarifies that 'Imam' in Surah Al-Isra 17:71 refers to the divinely appointed leader, emphasizing that spiritual security depends on recognizing him rather than the timing of his political rise. He asserts that those who die in the interim period are regarded as if they were standing in the Imam's camp or even martyred alongside the Prophet, highlighting the concept of *al-Intizar* (waiting) as an active state of allegiance. This underscores the Shia doctrine that knowledge of the Imam preserves one from the detriment of delayed authority.
